result.behaviour_summary: profiles.py gains CRYPTO_CLOSE = replace(CRYPTO, entry="close") and registers it as PROFILES["CRYPTO_CLOSE"] after the unchanged comprehension `{p.market: p for p in (IDX, US, CRYPTO)}`. The variant is field-for-field CRYPTO (0.1% fee + 0.1% tier per side, bands, lot 1, notional 5000, short carry 0.0005, both notes) except entry "close". Its .market field is deliberately "CRYPTO", not "CRYPTO_CLOSE": backtest.run keys the IDX/global branch, the sealed GLOBAL_HOLDOUT, the survivorship warning and summary["market"]["profile"] off profile.market, so a CRYPTO_CLOSE run is reported as profile CRYPTO / entry "close" and summary["config"]["market"] records "CRYPTO_CLOSE" (the RunConfig name) - verified by the run-level test. Nothing selects the variant unless a RunConfig names market="CRYPTO_CLOSE"; backtest.run reaches it today with no other change (PROFILES[cfg.market]). The dataclass, IDX, US and CRYPTO objects are untouched. Design note: I did not alter assumption_note/venue to label the variant, because the task specifies "differs only in entry_price"; the run label comes from config.market and market.entry in every summary.

open_concerns: Labelling: per the spec the variant is identical to CRYPTO except entry, so its assumption_note/venue do not mention the latency-pessimistic intent; the only in-run markers are summary.config.market == "CRYPTO_CLOSE" and summary.market.entry == "close" (summary.market.profile reads "CRYPTO"). If the E5 protocol wants the sensitivity named in the cost_assumption text, that is a one-field deviation from 'identical' to decide on explicitly.

Fill model: CRYPTO_CLOSE.entry == "close" makes execution.py:439 refuse fill_model "B" (open-only) and :441 refuse "C" unless units == "panel" and ca_mode == "registry" (crypto runs use ca_mode "adjusted"), so the variant runs with fill model A only, matching the protocol draft's 'A (as E2/E4 recorded runs)' for crypto; noted so no one expects B/C there.

Open-entry conditional plans: execution.py:415/420 tie some entry rules to entry_price (e.g. entry_rule "unlock" requires close; others may require open); a plan frozen for CRYPTO under open entry may not be valid under CRYPTO_CLOSE - the E5 harness should run resolve_plan + ExecConfig validation per profile rather than assume plan parity.
